summary: Split the over-length fake-client prompt-stream.ts by extracting addUserMessage/addAssistantMessage into a separate module, then ran the full verification suite (svelte-check, tsc, length check, app/agent-server/protocol tests) all clean. Rebuilt the app and relaunched the web server through the proper .gizmo-web/startup.cmd launcher, then smoke-tested the production build over the tunnel domain and accepted the origin. Added two memory notes (gizmo-web-server-startup, gizmo-headless-verification), updated MEMORY.md to index them, and restored the .gizmo-web/server.json state file so web:server:status tracks the running daemon. The assistant also confirmed eight earlier fixes shipped and are live.
decisions: Split addUserMessage/addAssistantMessage out of prompt-stream.ts into its own module to satisfy the 300-line file limit; this brought prompt-stream.ts down to 251 lines.
Relaunch the web server via .gizmo-web/startup.cmd rather than bare web:server:start, because the bare start drops the tunnel domain from the agent server's WebSocket origin allowlist.
Restore .gizmo-web/server.json by walking up the parent-process chain until the web-server.ts run process is found, so pnpm web:server:status/stop track the actual daemon.

Capture the always-on web server and headless verification workflows as durable memory notes (gizmo-web-server-startup.md, gizmo-headless-verification.md) indexed from MEMORY.md, including the note that the dev server on 5173 and the production launcher on 4173 cannot run concurrently because both want port 8787.
Use playwright-core loaded from nw_wrld's node_modules as the headless verification path when no preview MCP host is available, with `?fake` on Vite 5173 for dev and the tunnel domain for production.
errors: pnpm check:loc reported apps/app/src/lib/agent-client/fake-client/prompt-stream.ts had 309 lines and exceeded the 300-line limit; resolved by extracting the fake message-append methods into a sibling module.

Bare web:server:start dropped the tunnel domain from the agent server's WebSocket origin allowlist, causing the assistant's own connection error; fixed by relaunching through .gizmo-web/startup.cmd and confirming the domain origin is accepted again.

First Start-Process attempt for the launcher failed with 'The system cannot find the file specified' due to a path quoting issue; the subsequent invocation succeeded and the server came up listening on 4173 and 8787.

cat .gizmo-web/server.json returned 'No such file or directory' after the relaunch; resolved by walking the parent process tree to find the web-server.ts run process and rewriting server.json with its PID.
